doc.citation: García Muro, V.J., Rubinstein, C.V., Rustán, J.J. and Steemans, P. (2018). Palynomorphs from the Devonian Talacasto and Punta Negra Formations, Argentinean Precordillera: New biostratigraphic approach. Journal of South American Earth Sciences. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsames.2018.06.009
doc.comment: Extracted from the supplied accepted manuscript, including the PDF occurrence charts omitted from its text extraction. Fifty samples were studied; 26 levels yielded identifiable palynomorphs. Grey chart rectangles denote questionable occurrences and are identified in occurrence locators. Level 2 yielded only possible miospores; levels 42 and 45 have no spores plotted. Unidentifiable samples are not treated as demonstrated spore absences. Artemopyra brevicosta and Emphanisporites protophanus may be reworked. Upper Punta Negra ages remain uncertain, including disagreement with a Middle Devonian trilobite age. Five explicitly described earlier assemblages are included separately as literature summaries from Le Hérissé et al. (1997), García Muro et al. (2014a) and García Muro et al. (2017); these are partial lists, not newly analysed samples. Spores explicitly regarded as misidentified in Rubinstein (1999, 2000) are excluded. Chart, prose and caption differences are flagged without silently reconciling them.

items.locality: Loma de los Piojos, ca. 8 km southwest of Jáchal city, San Juan
items.depth_or_level: Level 1; sample 9930; 2 m below Keidel’s guide horizon
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore biostratigraphy, particularly ?Knoxisporites riondae, and correlation with the upper Talacasto succession; no independent precise age control.
items.setting_as_reported: muddy-shelf depositional system, developed during a high stand
items.notes: Few poorly preserved palynomorphs. The ?Knoxisporites riondae occurrence is questionable in Figure 3. Earlier faunal assignments extending the upper formation into the Emsian are disputed.

items.depth_or_level: Level 2; sample 9931; Keidel’s guide horizon
items.age_basis_detail: Horizon dated using regional palynological evidence and stratigraphic correlation; this sample itself yielded no recognizable palynomorphs.
items.setting_as_reported: muddy-shelf depositional system, developed during a high stand
items.notes: Some phytoclasts and possible miospores were recorded, but no recognizable palynomorphs. This is not a demonstrated spore absence.

items.locality: Loma de los Piojos, San Juan
items.depth_or_level: Level 15; sample 9943; approximately 230 m above Keidel’s horizon; uppermost studied Talacasto level
items.age_basis_detail: ?Knoxisporites riondae, Dictyotriletes emsiensis Morphon and other miospores; absence of taxa first appearing in the Emsian; correlation with Cerro La Chilca.
items.setting_as_reported: muddy-shelf depositional system, developed during a high stand; greenish gray siltstones and very fine sandstones
items.notes: Most abundant and diversified Talacasto assemblage: 10 miospore species, four microphytoplankton species and two freshwater acritarchs. Occurrence names follow Figure 3. Figure 6 captions instead use Dibolisporites sp., Dictyotriletes sp., Cymbohilates sp. and cf. Retusotriletes sp.; Figure 6.G misspells echinaceus as echinceus. These are not counted as additional taxa.

items.locality: Loma de los Piojos, San Juan
items.depth_or_level: Level 17; sample 10074; Belgian preparation 73782; basal pelitic interval
items.age_basis_detail: Lower pelitic interval considered consistent with the late Pragian age of the underlying Talacasto Formation; recognized palynomorphs could not directly date the basal Punta Negra.
items.setting_as_reported: light green mudstones; alternatively interpreted as submarine-fan, deltaic, or shallow marine deposits evolving towards turbiditic sandstone beds
items.notes: Artemopyra brevicosta may be reworked because its cited worldwide range is Wenlock–Lochkovian. Retusotriletes is questionable. Figure 5 uses Gneudnaspora divellomedia; the appendix identifies the recorded taxon as var. minor. The formation is marine-palynomorph dominated overall; its depositional interpretation is disputed.

items.depth_or_level: Level 32; sample 10090; near the transition from the approximately 210 m lower pelitic interval to coarser deposits
items.age_as_reported: an age younger than Pragian cannot be assumed
items.age_basis_detail: Cymbosporites proteus ranges from the Lochkovian MN Zone to the Emsian, but no Emsian markers were found. Conclusions favour consistency of the lower pelitic interval with late Pragian.
items.setting_as_reported: close to the coarser succession of intercalated greenish-gray wackes and siltstones
items.notes: Archaeozonotriletes chulus is questionable. Figure 5 also plots Emphanisporites protophanus here; section 4.1 discusses possible reworking of this species specifically at level 27. The proposed Pragian mapping follows the lower-interval interpretation and is not an independently established sample age.

items.age_basis_detail: Two specimens of Bimerga paulae, assigned a short late Pragian–early Emsian range.
items.setting_as_reported: coarser succession of intercalated greenish-gray wackes and siltstones
items.notes: Marine organic-walled microphytoplankton provides the principal age evidence and dominates the formation overall.

items.locality: Loma de los Piojos, San Juan

items.age_basis_detail: Formation-wide palynological assignment and stratigraphic position above the late Pragian/early Emsian level 33 and below Emsian levels 37–39; this sample is not precisely dated.
items.setting_as_reported: intercalated greenish-gray wackes and siltstones
items.notes: Latosporites sp. 1 has an Eifelian first appearance in Saudi Arabia, but the authors reject its use here as an age marker because of restricted geographic knowledge. Figure 5 and the appendix cite Breuer (2007), whereas the prose cites Breuer and Steemans (2013). The prose reports Archaeozonotriletes chulus at this level, while Figure 5 plots Archaeozonotriletes spp.; both reports are retained and may refer to the same material.

items.age_as_reported: a possible Emsian age should not be excluded
items.age_basis_detail: Schizocystia pilosa is used to question a post-Early Devonian age, whereas the trilobite Acanthopyge (Lobopyge) balliviani had supported a Middle Devonian assignment. Spores are considered insufficient for precise dating.
items.setting_as_reported: intercalated greenish-gray wackes and siltstones
items.notes: Age disputed; retained as a possible window assemblage rather than a secure Emsian record. Emphanisporites rotatus and Acinosporites sp. are questionable in Figure 5. The prose calls the latter cf. Acinosporites sp. The appendix identifies Gneudnaspora divellomedia as var. minor. Marine palynomorphs dominate the formation overall.

items.notes: The Early Devonian interpretation is tentative; a younger age for the uppermost formation remains possible. Figure 5 plots Retusotriletes spp., while the illustrated specimen is captioned Retusotriletes sp. Marine palynomorphs dominate the formation overall.

items.locality: Cerro del Fuerte, San Juan Precordillera
items.depth_or_level: lower part of the Talacasto Formation
items.age_basis_detail: Chitinozoan Urochitina loboi, acritarchs Demorhethium lappaceum and Schizocystia pilosa, and the listed trilete spores.
items.notes: Literature summary of Le Hérissé, Rubinstein and Steemans (1997), Lower Devonian palynomorphs from the Talacasto Formation, Cerro del Fuerte Section, San Juan Precordillera, Argentina. More than 50 palynomorph species were originally reported, but only these spores are named here. Dictyotiletes is the spelling in this paper’s discussion; the intended genus is identifiable elsewhere in the paper as Dictyotriletes.

items.locality: Río Jáchal
items.depth_or_level: uppermost 6.25 m of the Los Espejos Formation
items.age_basis_detail: Listed spores together with Schizocystia pilosa and Polyedryxium condensum; comparison with early Lochkovian MN and micrornatus-newportensis biozones.
items.notes: Literature summary of García Muro, Rubinstein and Steemans (2014a), Palynological record of the Silurian/Devonian boundary in the Argentine Precordillera, western Gondwana. These are the spores named in the present paper, not a complete re-extraction of the earlier study. Cymbosporites paulus? is followed in the text by in Wellman (1993).

items.locality: Río Jáchal
items.depth_or_level: basal 31.5 m of the Talacasto Formation
items.age_basis_detail: Palynological boundary placement in the underlying Los Espejos Formation; listed Talacasto spores considered consistent with the Lochkovian assignment.
items.notes: Literature summary of García Muro et al. (2014a). The two spores are explicitly assigned to the lower Talacasto section. This is a partial list quoted by the present paper.

items.locality: Cerro La Chilca
items.depth_or_level: lower 15 m of the Talacasto Formation
items.age_basis_detail: Schizocystia pilosa, Winwaloeusia distracta and Dictyotriletes emsiensis Morphon.
items.notes: Literature summary of García Muro, Rubinstein and Rustán (2017), Early Devonian organic-walled phytoplankton and miospores from the Precordillera Basin of San Juan, Argentina: biostratigraphic and paleobiogeographic implications. The earlier assemblages were dominated by marine organic-walled microphytoplankton; only the spore named in this summary is extracted.

items.locality: Cerro La Chilca
items.depth_or_level: upper 850 m of the sequence
items.age_basis_detail: Organic-walled microphytoplankton, including Palacanthus ledanoisii and Polyedryxium cf. P. decorum, together with the listed spores.
items.notes: Literature summary of García Muro et al. (2017), not newly analysed material. These ages conflict with earlier faunal schemes placing the Lochkovian/Pragian boundary much higher and assigning the upper Talacasto to the Emsian. Earlier assemblages were marine-microphytoplankton dominated; the list here contains only the spores named in this paper’s summary.
